reviewFlags.note: Stress Resilience (adaptive capacity) vs Stress Reactivity (response intensity) — related but not identical; do not merge automatically.
Motivation/Drive vs Behavioural Activation — related; remain separate unless manually merged.
Emotional Regulation (affective modulation) vs Apprehensive Worry (sustained apprehensive/ruminative cognition) — RDoC Negative Valence / cognitive control overlap; remain separate.

Reward Regulation (sensitivity, learning, seeking) vs Pleasure & Interest Capacity (experienced interest/pleasure and consummatory engagement) — RDoC Positive Valence / anhedonia domain; remain separate.
Emotional Regulation vs Social Engagement Capacity (affiliation, approach, participation) — RDoC Social Processes; remain separate.

relationships.rationale: Serotonin signalling intersects negative-valence and control circuits discussed in mood and anxiety contexts {{cite:briguglio_dietary_2018}}. Systemic-inflammation connectivity is not a serotonin measurement {{cite:marsland_systemic_2017}}.

GABAergic inhibition is relevant to anxiety-related processes, providing a plausible biological connection to Apprehensive Worry. The closest human trial found that high-dose vitamin B6 reduced self-reported anxiety and strengthened an inhibitory visual assay, but it measured neither GABA nor GABA synthesis {{cite:field_high-dose_2022}}. No study here directly assessed worry, rumination or perseverative thought, while GAD65-deficient mice show sex-dependent rather than uniform anxiety-like changes {{cite:ulrich_sex_2023}}.

Systemic inflammation associates with default-mode network connectivity patterns linked to perseverative thought in translational anxiety/depression framing; NF-κB transcriptional tone is the mechanism boundary.

Gut–brain microbiota signalling modulates central GABA receptor expression and anxiety-related behaviour in animal models; gut-derived inflammatory load may intersect apprehensive-worry biology in anxiety/depression comorbidity framing.

Persistent inflammatory signalling through IL-6- and TNF-α-linked cytokine networks is a recognised contributor to anxious and perseverative cognition within neuroimmune framing (Slavich & Irwin, 2014; Marsland et al., 2017). Human omega-3 intervention reduced inflammatory markers and anxiety symptoms alongside resolution-phase cytokine remodelling (Kiecolt-Glaser et al., 2011; Ferguson et al., 2014). This PM governs cytokine-network tone — not omega-3 treatment — and attached anxiety outcomes require one inferential step to PH016 rather than direct perseverative-thought measurement.

Persistent inflammatory signalling and impaired resolution-phase lipid mediator balance are recognised contributors to anxious perseverative cognition within neuroimmune framing (Slavich & Irwin, 2014; Marsland et al., 2017). SPM-oriented resolution biology and human omega-3 intervention reduced inflammatory markers and anxiety symptoms alongside cytokine remodelling (Kiecolt-Glaser et al., 2011; Ferguson et al., 2014). This PM governs eicosanoid–SPM balance — not omega-3 treatment — and attached anxiety outcomes require one inferential step to PH016 rather than direct perseverative-thought measurement.
Endocannabinoid–dopamine coupling may influence behavioural activation and effort-related signalling context relevant to ADHD framing.
Omega-3-derived ethanolamides may support neuroprotective and neurogenesis-related signalling context relevant to cognitive clarity without CB1-centric framing.
Oestrogen influences neural signalling systems relevant to cognitive stability across menstrual and perimenopausal contexts; ADHD-specific outcome claims should remain cautious.
Altered oestrogen recycling may indirectly influence neural signalling context relevant to cognitive clarity without establishing direct single-pathway outcome certainty.

Cholinergic signalling is a biological context for working-memory and cognitive precision {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}} {{cite:briguglio_dietary_2018}}. The attached sources do not measure cognitive-clarity scores after a choline change aimed at acetylcholine synthesis.

DHA in neuronal phospholipids supports membrane architecture used in synaptic signalling {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}} {{cite:patrick_role_2019}}. Delivery form can change accretion in an animal model {{cite:liu_higher_2014}}. Those are structural and transport findings, not cognitive-clarity scores after a human DHA change.
Efficient glutamate uptake and recycling terminate excitatory signalling {{cite:zhou_glutamate_2014}}. The attached sources do not measure cognitive-clarity outcomes in ADHD cohorts.

Folic acid, with or without vitamin B12, lowers blood homocysteine {{cite:collaboration_lowering_1998}}. In older adults with mild cognitive impairment, B-vitamin treatment was associated with slower cognitive decline only when omega-3 status was higher {{cite:oulhaj_omega-3_2016}}. Blood homocysteine and that combined B-vitamin interaction do not measure methionine synthase flux, and they do not establish that this reaction itself changes cognitive clarity.

Lower plasma homocysteine after betaine supplements is a blood measurement, not a test of cognitive clarity or of tissue BHMT activity {{cite:olthof_low_2003}}. A choline review discusses neurodevelopment rather than an effect of this reaction on clarity {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. The relationship remains an indirect bridge with no direct outcome evidence.

SAMe supplies methyl groups used by many downstream pathways relevant to neural function, but this is an inferred downstream bridge rather than evidence that MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis itself modulates Cognitive Clarity. The attached methylation review establishes SAMe's donor role, not a cognitive outcome or endogenous synthesis-flux effect {{cite:chiang_s-adenosylmethionine_1996}}. Circulating SAMe or SAM:SAH measurements cannot isolate MAT synthesis from utilisation and clearance {{cite:corrillero_bravo_analysis_2022}}. Direct relationship evidence remains a gap.

SAM donates methyl groups, and homocysteine is then split between remethylation and transsulfuration {{cite:chiang_s-adenosylmethionine_1996,finkelstein_homocysteine_1998}}. Homocysteine concentration is discussed as a risk marker for cognitive decline and Alzheimer disease {{cite:luzzi_homocysteine_2022,yu_evidence-based_2020}}. Those studies measure a metabolite level. They do not measure branch rates, and they do not show that changing cycle throughput improves Cognitive Clarity.

SAMe-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation couples one-carbon methylation to membrane phospholipid chemistry — the methylation-dependent bridge between B-vitamin status and omega-3-enriched PC delivery toward the brain. VITACOG reanalysis, PEMT pathway biology, and phospholipid-bound DHA accretion evidence support cognitive-clarity framework translation. The findings support an association with cognitive outcomes, while the proposed causal role of methylation–membrane coupling remains unproven. Applicability to ADHD has not yet been established.
Polyphenol-rich dietary patterns and lower pro-inflammatory signalling pressure may support cognitive clarity context in ADHD-relevant populations without single-nutrient outcome claims.
Butyrate and gut-barrier context may reduce neuroinflammation and support brain energy metabolism — translational links to cognitive clarity without direct ADHD treatment-efficacy claims.
Verlaet reviews a rationale for dietary antioxidant treatment in ADHD. The human measurement is nasal defence-gene expression after a prepared sprout homogenate, not a cognitive result.
Thiol/disulfide shifts and DNA oxidation markers in ADHD adults support state-sensitive redox interpretation relevant to cognitive clarity without diagnostic claims.
One adult cohort had higher malondialdehyde. That marker is not a vitamin E result. Lutein is not the chain-breaking antioxidant in this membrane reaction.
Synergistic antioxidant network regeneration may support cognitive clarity context in ADHD oxidative-load framing better than isolated megadose antioxidants.
Postprandial inflammatory patterns in ADHD metabolic overlap may modulate cognitive clarity through cytokine-network context rather than single-mechanism claims.
Specialized pro-resolving mediators actively terminate inflammation without suppressing immune surveillance — supporting cognitive clarity context through resolution-oriented lipid signalling.

ADHD-focused gut–brain axis review literature synthesises microbiome ecology research gaps — indirect cognitive-clarity framing through microbial community resilience rather than measured clarity outcomes.

Gut-derived polyphenol metabolites may influence mitochondrial and inflammatory resilience with downstream cognitive implications — framework translation from ADHD gut–brain research gaps rather than direct clarity-outcome measurement.
Insulin sensitivity and metabolic stability interact with reproductive hormone regulation; this PM should be framed as metabolic-endocrine integration rather than a direct ADHD treatment claim.
Low testosterone states are associated with reduced energy, fatigue and reduced mental stamina, but direct ADHD-specific evidence remains limited.
Microbial androgen metabolism may influence systemic androgen exposure relevant to energy and stamina context; direct ADHD evidence remains limited.

Dopamine can influence willingness to sustain cognitive effort, but the strongest assessed human study measured effort choice rather than fatigue or performance decline over time {{cite:westbrook_dopamine_2020}}. Cognitive energy remains a multi-system outcome, and a dopamine-specific fatigue claim is unresolved.

The same cybrid cells respired less, which is consistent with less ATP-generating capacity in that model {{cite:verma_attention_2016}}. Cognitive energy was not measured, and the result is not a meal prescription.

Cybrid cells carrying platelet mitochondria from three boys with ADHD respired less, but NAD⁺ was not measured {{cite:verma_attention_2016}}. A review of ADHD mitochondrial papers does not add an NAD⁺ measurement {{cite:ogutlu_mitochondrial_2023}}.

Creatine–phosphocreatine buffering is positioned to stabilise ATP supply during changing demand. In a small crossover trial during acute sleep deprivation, a high single creatine dose altered cerebral high-energy phosphate measures and partially preserved cognitive performance {{cite:gordji-nejad_creatine_sleep_2024}}. This supports a conditional relationship under acute metabolic stress, not a universal energy effect.

Carnitine-dependent fat oxidation supports mitochondrial substrate delivery for ATP production — trial evidence in ADHD children links this transport node to functional improvement alongside behavioural endpoints.

ADHD mitochondrial dysfunction reviews describe substrate-flexibility strain when oxidative phosphorylation is impaired — ketone utilisation is an indirect alternative-fuel pathway node without ADHD ketone-intervention outcomes in the hub set.

Narrative synthesis of ADHD mitochondrial biomarker and oxidative-stress literature supports fuel-switching flexibility as a modifiable bioenergetic context when respiration is compromised — direct ADHD fuel-switching outcome trials remain limited.

PET evidence of altered cerebral glucose metabolism in adults with hyperactivity of childhood onset and unhealthy dietary pattern associations with ADHD in case–control path analysis converge on meal-level glucose appearance kinetics as a cognitive-energy node.

Altered cerebral glucose metabolism in ADHD and metabolic syndrome/insulin-resistance overlap in adult ADHD outpatients support glycaemic variability as a modifiable context for steadier cognitive fuel supply.

Insulin resistance and ADHD metabolic overlap reviewed in narrative synthesis support efficient glucose disposal as a contributor to cognitive fuel stability — mechanism boundary is peripheral/metabolic insulin action, not CNS glucose transport pharmacology.
Dietary NAPE and NAE precursor biology may modulate endocannabinoidome context relevant to affective regulation; direct ADHD outcome claims remain cautious.
Omega-3 endocannabinoidome signalling may indirectly modulate affective context through inflammatory and neuromodulatory interfaces; direct ADHD evidence remains limited.
Preserved anandamide signalling may modulate affective regulation pathways through endogenous tone rather than receptor agonism.
Stress-buffering endocannabinoidome signalling may modulate affective regulation through mood-disorder-relevant endocannabinoid pathways.
Oestrogen-mediated signalling may modulate affective regulation pathways that intersect with dopaminergic tone and stress sensitivity.

The estrobolome can influence systemic oestrogen exposure through microbial beta-glucuronidase activity; downstream affective phenome effects are indirect and should not be presented as single-mechanism causal claims.
Butyrate-producing taxa may support endocrine and inflammatory contexts relevant to progesterone balance, but direct ADHD outcome evidence is limited.
Metabolic volatility may indirectly influence affective regulation through neuroendocrine and reproductive hormone coupling.
Androgen signalling may influence mood and emotional regulation through interactions with multiple neural systems.
Microbiome-androgen interactions may influence endocrine states relevant to mood and behavioural regulation, but direct ADHD evidence is currently limited.
Tryptophan is an indispensable amino acid and the serotonin precursor. Coverage of that amino acid is not a measurement of emotional regulation, and serotonin signalling is a later step.

Carbohydrate-rich versus protein-rich meals can change the plasma tryptophan-to-LNAA ratio {{cite:wurtman_effects_2003,ashley_breakfast_1985,fernstrom_lnna_2013}}. Plasma-ratio change is not serotonin signalling or an emotional-regulation benefit.

Serotonin signalling is a core biological substrate for emotional regulation, impulse control and affective stability {{cite:shaw_emotion_2014}}. ADHD-focused serotonin reviews do not establish a uniform serotonin deficit that diet can correct {{cite:faraone_serotonin_2025}} {{cite:banerjee_does_2015}}.

Combined omega-3/6 with magnesium and zinc was followed by fewer emotional-problem scores in an observational ADHD-seeking cohort {{cite:huss_supplementation_2010}}. Membrane DHA remains the mechanism boundary; the multi-nutrient design cannot isolate incorporation {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}}.

GABA contributes to inhibitory neural processes involved in behavioural and emotional regulation. Human studies link GABA concentrations in relevant brain regions with impulsivity and aggression {{cite:ende_impulsivity_2016}}, supporting the relevance of GABA biology to Emotional Regulation. However, these studies measure GABA concentration rather than synthesis rate {{cite:mason_decrease_2001,manor_rate_1996}}, and direct human evidence connecting GABA synthesis capacity itself with Emotional Regulation is currently lacking.

SAMe-dependent methylation is biologically relevant to downstream neurotransmitter and membrane chemistry, but the attached mood-disorder review concerns exogenous SAMe and combined folate/B12 treatment rather than endogenous MAT activity or SAMe synthesis flux {{cite:cicero_combined_2022}}. It therefore does not directly demonstrate that this PM modulates Emotional Regulation; the relationship remains an indirect framework bridge with a direct-evidence gap.
Systemic inflammatory signalling may intersect affective regulation framing in neurodevelopmental contexts; this PM governs transcriptional inflammatory tone only—not downstream cytokine phenotypes.
Low-grade endotoxemia and sustained systemic inflammation correlate with mood instability in translational framing; gut-derived load remains the boundary of this spillover step.
Oxidative stress intersects neuroinflammatory cascades relevant to affective dysregulation framing; net redox balance is the mechanism boundary for this PM.
Oxidative membrane damage and mitochondrial overlap may intersect affective regulation in neurodevelopmental framing; scope remains lipid-peroxidation control only.
Network antioxidant sufficiency may indirectly modulate affective context under chronic oxidative stress; high-dose single-nutrient supplementation shows inconsistent benefit.
Omega-3-derived resolution biology may modulate affective inflammatory context when EPA/DHA substrate and omega-6:omega-3 balance are adequate over habitual intake.

The attached ADHD microbiota study did not measure intestinal permeability, tight-junction function or emotional-regulation outcomes {{cite:jiang_gut_2018}}. No direct evidence in the bounded assessment established that this PM modulates Emotional Regulation, so this remains a framework-level hypothesis with a direct-evidence gap.

SCFA gut–brain signalling may intersect affective regulation through vagal and immune pathways — indirect translational framing from ADHD SCFA deficit observation without emotional-outcome intervention trials.

Probiotic-associated symptom change in ADHD children and hypothesis-generating early-life microbial modulation windows support gut–vagal pathways intersecting affective regulation biology without definitive prevention claims.

Cortisol, inflammatory biomarkers, and neurotrophins measured in children and adolescents with ADHD intersect affective regulation biology through HPA-axis tone — this PM governs cortisol rhythm, not autonomic recovery (FM3).
Oestrogen influences dopaminergic and neural signalling systems relevant to executive function; direct single-mechanism ADHD outcome claims should remain cautious.

Meal protein supplies circulating phenylalanine, and phenylalanine can be converted to tyrosine. Tyrosine and tryptophan are precursors later catecholamine and serotonin pathways can use. These studies do not measure attention.

Meal-level LNAA competition at LAT1 can shift plasma tyrosine and tryptophan ratios and, on review evidence, brain-entry bias {{cite:fernstrom_lnna_2013,ashley_breakfast_1985,wurtman_effects_2003}}. The attached meal studies do not measure attention or ADHD outcomes, and transport modulation cannot substitute for substrate sufficiency or downstream signalling.

Dopamine contributes to working memory and cognitive control, but the relationship is nonlinear and depends on baseline state and whether prefrontal stability or striatal updating is required {{cite:cools_inverted-u_2011}}. ADHD imaging findings are heterogeneous across dopamine processes, regions and medication histories rather than showing a uniform dopamine deficit {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024,fusar-poli_striatal_2012}}.

Noradrenaline helps set arousal and vigilance so attention and executive control can stay engaged {{cite:odonnell_norepinephrine_2012}}. That biological role is not a dietary-treatment claim, and ADHD imaging that varies by dopamine process does not show a uniform noradrenaline deficit or a food-based attention effect {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}.

Acetylcholine is the cholinergic transmitter used in attention and learning circuits {{cite:johansson_decreased_2013}} {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. Receptor-binding differences in boys with ADHD and choline/neurodevelopment reviews supply translational context. They do not show that changing choline intake treats ADHD or raises brain acetylcholine.

Membrane DHA is a structural context for synaptic signalling {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}}. An observational multi-nutrient study in children seeking help for ADHD-related symptoms cannot isolate membrane DHA from co-supplemented minerals {{cite:huss_supplementation_2010}}. Omega-3 ADHD reviews remain contextual {{cite:pei-chen_chang_personalised_2021}}.

Regional glutamate/glutamine measures associate with attention scores in adults with ADHD {{cite:maltezos_glutamateglutamine_2014}}. That is a spectroscopic pool link, not measured excitatory amino-acid transporter flux. Uptake and recycling terminate excitatory signalling {{cite:zhou_glutamate_2014}}.

Children with ADHD have been reported to have lower folate and vitamin B12 than comparison groups, and one cohort of boys also had higher homocysteine {{cite:razavinia_vitamins_2024,lukovac_serum_2024,wang_dietary_2019}}. Those are observational blood and diet differences. They do not show that methionine synthase activity is lower, and they do not show that folate or vitamin B12 supplementation improves attention. An MTHFR polymorphism meta-analysis concerns a folate-cycle enzyme upstream of this reaction, not methionine synthase flux {{cite:meng_association_2022}}.

Reviews of ADHD diets and of choline in neurodevelopment discuss attention, but they do not test BHMT activity or betaine supplementation as an attention treatment {{cite:millichap_diet_2012,derbyshire_role_2023}}. The enzyme reaction is established separately, and a change in plasma homocysteine is not an attention outcome {{cite:evans_betaine_2002,olthof_low_2003}}. Direct evidence that this remethylation route changes Focus / Attention Stability remains a gap.

Boys with ADHD had higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 than controls, and a separate case-control study linked less healthy diets with lower folate, vitamin B6 and vitamin B12 and with ADHD {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024,wang_dietary_2019}}. Those are concentration and dietary-pattern associations. They do not measure remethylation or transsulfuration rates {{cite:finkelstein_homocysteine_1998,lamers_vitamin_b6_methionine_cycle_2011}}.

Diet and choline reviews discuss attention and neurodevelopment {{cite:millichap_diet_2012}} {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. They do not measure PEMT activity. Piglet brain DHA accretion and human cerebrospinal-fluid DHA likewise do not record this methylation {{cite:liu_higher_2014}} {{cite:arellanes_brain_2020}}. Any attention relationship is a downstream inference.

Postprandial and LPS-linked inflammatory signalling intersects ADHD metabolic overlap — pattern-based anti-inflammatory meals may modulate attention-relevant inflammatory tone rather than acute NF-κB pharmacology.

Propionate protected an in vitro blood–brain barrier model. That is not endotoxin translocation, and it is not an attention result. Gut microbiota studies in children remain context for this spillover step.
The human exposure changed phase II enzyme RNA in nasal cells. It does not show that ordinary repeated eating changes attention, and the sources do not compare repeated exposure with a single dose.
Elevated oxidative stress indices and lipid-peroxidation markers in adult and paediatric ADHD cohorts may modulate attention-relevant redox burden when generation exceeds clearance.
Lipid-peroxidation burden tracks oxidative load in ADHD cohorts; food-state antioxidant coverage may modulate membrane protection relevant to sustained attention contexts.

Youth ADHD cohort work reported higher hs-CRP and IL-6 with lower TNF-α, BDNF and bedtime cortisol — a mixed peripheral immune–neuroendocrine pattern rather than uniform pro-inflammatory cytokine elevation; omega-3 interventions reshape resolution-phase cytokine responses.
Resolution-phase lipid mediator balance may intersect attention-relevant inflammatory tone; direct ADHD SPM outcome evidence remains limited.

Cybrid cells carrying platelet mitochondria from three boys with ADHD had lower respiration, lower complex V activity, a lower membrane potential and higher mitochondrial superoxide than control cybrids {{cite:verma_attention_2016}}. That is a small cell model. It does not show that diet changes attention.

Controlled carnitine supplementation improved behavioural and functional outcomes in children with ADHD — the strongest direct ADHD intervention anchor in BRS4, mapping fatty-acid transport into mitochondria to attention-relevant outcomes without generalising beyond trial context.

Serum zonulin was associated with hyperactivity scores in one small cross-sectional ADHD study {{cite:ozyurt_increased_2018}}, but serum zonulin is an indirect barrier marker and the design cannot establish that tight-junction integrity causes attention instability. The attached microbiota-composition study did not measure permeability or tight junctions {{cite:jiang_gut_2018}}. The PM → Phenome relationship therefore remains indirect and observational.

Gut microbiota profiles and an inflammatory marker have been compared with attention-related scores. [[5]](#pm-ref-5) [[7]](#pm-ref-7) Those studies did not measure lipopolysaccharide or endotoxin containment, so they do not show that this exposure mechanism changes attention.

Reduced microbial alpha diversity in paediatric ADHD, compositional shifts in treatment-naïve cohorts, and open-label Bifidobacterium supplementation with symptom change converge on ecological keystone support as attention-relevant gut–brain context.

Reduced microbial alpha diversity in paediatric ADHD and lower faecal SCFA levels versus controls support ecological turnover and competitive selection as modifiable gut-community processes intersecting attention-relevant microbiome structure.

ADHD cohorts showed lower faecal SCFA levels including acetic, propionic, isobutyric, isovaleric, and valeric acids versus controls — positioning microbial SCFA production and signalling as a direct observational anchor for attention-relevant gut metabolite biology.

ADHD microbiota compositional differences and lower SCFA levels imply altered microbial biotransformation of dietary precursors relevant to gut–brain neurotransmitter availability — mechanism boundary is microbial precursor processing, not BRS1 monoamine synthesis.

Dietary pattern linked to ADHD burden implicates postprandial glucose dynamics intersecting prefrontal and striatal fuel supply relevant to attention biology — this PM governs glucose appearance rate, not insulin disposal (PM3) or variability amplitude (PM2).
Prefrontal glucose utilisation patterns in ADHD and metabolic comorbidity prevalence link glycaemic fluctuation control to attention-relevant cognitive energy availability.
Estrobolome activity may support or disrupt oestrogen exposure depending on microbial beta-glucuronidase balance and enterohepatic recycling direction.
Insulin-linked metabolic signalling and gut ecological context may modulate oestrogen-progesterone balance across feeding and stress cycles.
NAPE → NAE biosynthesis may support AEA, PEA, and OEA signalling context relevant to motivation and drive through diet-actionable endocannabinoidome pathways rather than CB1 receptor pharmacology.
Endocannabinoid signalling modulates dopaminergic reward and motivation pathways; this PM addresses neuromodulation rather than dopamine production.
Testosterone signalling has been associated with motivation, effort, behavioural activation and goal-directed behaviour.
Microbial androgen metabolism may influence systemic androgen availability and indirectly influence motivation-related phenomes.
Phenylalanine from dietary protein can be converted to tyrosine, the dopamine precursor. That supply is not a measurement of motivation or drive, and it is not dopaminergic signalling.

Protein-forward meals can raise the plasma tyrosine ratio relative to competing LNAAs {{cite:wurtman_effects_2003,fernstrom_lnna_2013}}. That is precursor-presentation bias, not a motivation, drive or ADHD outcome; signalling belongs downstream of this PM.

Striatal dopamine synthesis capacity and controlled dopaminergic manipulation alter willingness to expend cognitive effort by changing benefit-versus-cost weighting, supporting a direct relationship with effort allocation rather than a general “reward chemical” account {{cite:westbrook_dopamine_2020}}.

Noradrenaline can change arousal and effort-related tone, but dopaminergic reward circuitry remains the primary biological driver of Motivation / Drive {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}. The attached sources do not measure motivation after a dietary change, and iron-deficiency reviews are not motivation trials {{cite:beard_iron_2003}}.

Gut microbiome composition linked to neural reward anticipation in ADHD positions keystone taxa support as a biological node intersecting motivation-relevant gut–brain signalling — not a direct reward-intervention claim.

Microbial metabolite handling intersects reward-anticipation biology linked to gut composition in ADHD — indirect motivation framing through precursor/metabolite availability rather than direct drive-outcome trials.

Dietary pattern associations with ADHD burden and HPA dysregulation support stress-modulated reward/motivation pathways — mechanism boundary is appetite–reward drive under stress, not BRS1 catecholamine synthesis.

Catecholamine systems can sit near reward and incentive-motivation biology, but the attached insulin–dopamine review does not measure noradrenaline signalling or a pleasure outcome after diet {{cite:gruber_impact_2023}}. Dopamine-process heterogeneity in ADHD is not a pleasure-capacity finding for this mechanism {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}.

Serotonin pathways sit near positive-valence mood biology {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. Saffron supplementation trials are not serotonin-process measurements and are not a Dietary Requirement of this mechanism {{cite:jackson_effects_2021}}.

LPS-linked neurotransmission disruption intersects depressive mood biology in translational reviews; pro-inflammatory transcriptional tone may modulate this context without direct anhedonia-outcome claims.

Mitochondrial dysfunction is a recurrent theme in depression pathophysiology reviews; cytokine-network inflammatory tone may intersect reward-related mitochondrial biology without a direct anhedonia measurement.

Resolution-phase eicosanoid balance may modulate inflammatory tone intersecting reward-processing and depressive biology in translational framing; Gruber et al. (2023) reviews insulin–dopamine reward disruption in depression as adjacent context.
Endocannabinoid-mediated stress buffering may support recovery from stress-linked neuroinflammatory and excitatory load; direct ADHD evidence remains limited.

This mapping is translational. Limiting chronic receptor-driven energy stress could sit near recovery after load, but Clerc et al. did not measure human recovery outcomes. The relationship remains low-confidence {{cite:clerc_magnesium_2013}}.

Cysteine released by cystathionine cleavage can be used later for glutathione synthesis, which is a separate mechanism. The enzyme studies do not measure recovery capacity, and they do not show that changing this conversion treats recovery {{cite:zhu_cgl_kinetics_2008,steegborn_cgl_kinetics_1999}}.

Glutathione assembly supplies a thiol used in cellular redox buffering, which is relevant to recovery only as downstream biology. The human synthesis measurements are erythrocyte kinetics after combined precursor supplementation in older adults, not a recovery-outcome trial {{cite:sekhar_glutathione_2011}}. A sulfur-amino-acid-free diet slowed whole-blood synthesis while concentration was maintained {{cite:lyons_glutathione_2000}}. Higher homocysteine in boys with ADHD does not measure glutathione synthesis or recovery {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.
The ADHD mitochondrial review discusses mitochondrial strain. It does not measure recovery, and it does not measure NAD⁺ {{cite:ogutlu_mitochondrial_2023}}.

Rapid ATP buffering is biologically relevant to recovery after energetic demand, but the reviewed human evidence primarily measures cerebral creatine, cognition during acute stress, or clinical contexts rather than recovery capacity itself {{cite:dolan_beyond_muscle_2019}}. The relationship therefore remains indirect and evidence-limited.

Elevated glutathione and oxidative-stress markers in paediatric ADHD case–control work link mitochondrial ROS handling to redox recovery context; GSH is required for mitochondrial lactate metabolism and ROS neutralisation — this PM governs ROS production/control balance, not GSH synthesis (BRS2/BRS3).

Integrated mitochondrial membrane protection and redox integrity preserve energetic output when oxidative stress is elevated in paediatric ADHD — convergent with Verlaet glutathione/oxidative-stress findings and ADHD mitophagy reviews.

ADHD mitophagy and mitochondrial quality-control reviews link biogenesis/adaptation biology to long-term energetic restoration after repeated metabolic demand — diet and training provide permissive substrate context; direct ADHD biogenesis-outcome trials remain sparse.

Microbial polyphenol biotransformation generates mitophagy-relevant metabolites bridging BRS5 to BRS4 — ADHD hub evidence for this PM is indirect via gut–brain axis review context; direct ADHD urolithin-outcome trials are not in the curated set (biology > evidence gap).

Parasympathetic recovery after sympathetic activation is the mechanism boundary for restoring autonomic balance following challenge — Lane autonomic differentiation work provides ADHD-relevant context.

Metabolic-inflammatory load allocation may constrain recovery after sustained metabolic or stress challenge — indirect translation from ADHD–metabolic disorder synthesis rather than measured recovery outcomes.
Endocannabinoid modulation of mesolimbic dopamine signalling may influence reward regulation without equating to substance reward pharmacology.

Serotonin can interact with dopaminergic reward circuits and behavioural inhibition {{cite:faraone_serotonin_2025}}. That interaction is not a measured reward outcome after diet {{cite:tang_nutritional_2025}}.
Unhealthy dietary pattern linked to ADHD in case–control path analysis and altered cortisol patterns in ADHD youth intersect stress-driven appetite and reward regulation biology.
Progesterone-linked calming tone may intersect with gut-derived inflammatory and SCFA signalling, but evidence for direct dietary single-mechanism effects remains limited.
Serotonin participates in sleep–wake and calming neurochemistry {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. Meal-level precursor transport is not a sleep outcome {{cite:fernstrom_lnna_2013}}.

GABAergic inhibition supports calming neurophysiology relevant to sleep and arousal balance. In adults with polysomnography-verified primary insomnia, brain GABA concentration has been compared with good sleepers in three independent samples, reporting lower, higher, and null group differences {{cite:winkelman_reduced_2008,morgan_cortical_2012,spiegelhalder_magnetic_2016}}. However, the human findings are inconsistent, and these studies measure GABA concentration rather than GABA synthesis capacity.
Vagal tone intersects calming and sleep-relevant autonomic tone — indirect framing from ADHD autonomic differentiation literature without direct sleep-intervention outcomes.

Serotonin can modulate affiliative and social-affective behaviour in translational accounts {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. A saffron social-relationship outcome is not a serotonin signalling measurement {{cite:jackson_effects_2021}}.

GABAergic regulation may influence Social Engagement indirectly through processes such as arousal and threat processing. In mice, lifelong loss of GAD65 increased preference for social interaction partners in both sexes {{cite:ulrich_sex_2023}}, opposite to a simple expectation that reduced GABA synthesis would reduce social approach. There is no human evidence linking GABA synthesis capacity to social engagement, and rodent partner preference is not equivalent to human social capacity.

Gut–brain GABAergic modulation has been linked to reduced anxiety- and depression-related behaviour in preclinical models; social-engagement outcomes remain indirect translational inference for this gut-inflammatory PM.
Microbial SCFA context may indirectly influence stress-responsive endocrine-inflammatory tone intersecting progesterone-related stability.

This mapping is translational. Injury-level glutamate-receptor stress can sit near how systems react under load, but the attached work does not measure human stress-reactivity outcomes. Clerc et al. used a preclinical chronic receptor-stimulation model, so the relationship remains low-confidence {{cite:clerc_magnesium_2013}}.

Homocysteine can be joined to serine and then cleaved to cysteine, but that chemistry is not evidence of a stress-reactivity effect. A study of boys with ADHD found higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12. It did not measure these enzymes, cysteine production, or stress outcomes, and it is not a treatment result {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.

Oxidative-stress elevation in ADHD cohorts intersects stress-relevant redox tone — impaired ROS control may modulate allostatic load under repeated challenge without claiming oxidative stress causes ADHD.

The same studies did not measure lipopolysaccharide. [[5]](#pm-ref-5) [[7]](#pm-ref-7) They do not show that endotoxin containment changes stress reactivity. The supporting finding is recorded with Focus / Attention Stability.

Meta-analysis reports altered basal and morning cortisol patterns in youths with ADHD; cortisol levels in children with ADHD and sensory-over-responsivity differentiation work using cortisol markers converge on HPA rhythm as a stress-reactivity node.

Sensory over-responsivity differentiated from ADHD using electrodermal responses, cortisol, and anxiety markers; cortisol and inflammatory biomarkers in ADHD youth support autonomic activation/recovery balance as a stress-reactivity node.
PEA and related NAEs may intersect with stress-buffering endocannabinoidome signalling; dietary phospholipid support remains the primary intervention frame.
DHEA and related omega-3 ethanolamides may intersect with anti-inflammatory and stress-buffering endocannabinoidome pathways.
FAAH inhibition may preserve endogenous anandamide tone relevant to stress-buffering context; dietary polyphenols such as genistein represent plausible diet-sensitive modulation points.
The endocannabinoidome appears more relevant to stress buffering than direct cognitive enhancement, integrating neuroinflammatory, HPA, and glutamatergic regulation context.

Serotonin signalling participates in emotional processing and stress-related control {{cite:shaw_emotion_2014}}. The attached sources do not measure stress resilience after a dietary change aimed at serotonin {{cite:tang_nutritional_2025}}.

The same thiol pool is a plausible contributor to stress buffering, but no assessed study tested a stress-resilience outcome {{cite:sekhar_glutathione_2011,lyons_glutathione_2000}}. The paediatric ADHD biomarker study measured homocysteine and vitamin B12, not glutathione synthesis or stress resilience {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.
Nrf2-dependent detoxification and antioxidant gene programmes may intersect stress-buffering redox context; direct ADHD stress-outcome evidence remains limited.

Compensatory glutathione elevation in ADHD may reflect network activity under oxidative burden; polyphenol–fibre patterns supporting urolithin A context may modulate stress-buffering redox resilience.

Mitophagy and mitochondrial quality-control biology reviewed in ADHD contexts support redox-resilience framing when oxidative insult is recurrent — mechanism boundary is organelle integrity, not pharmacological antioxidant treatment claims.

Open-label Bifidobacterium bifidum supplementation associated with symptom change and altered gut microbiota in children with ADHD — vagal/ENS signalling is the proposed gut–brain conduit; early-life Lactobacillus exposure adds developmental modulation context.

Electrodermal and autonomic markers differentiate sensory over-responsivity from ADHD — vagal tone/HRV regulation is the parasympathetic arm supporting stress-buffering capacity in neurodevelopmental autonomic profiling.

BRS1(FM1).evidence_summary: Serotonin signalling intersects negative-valence and control circuits discussed in mood and anxiety contexts {{cite:briguglio_dietary_2018}}. Systemic-inflammation connectivity is not a serotonin measurement {{cite:marsland_systemic_2017}}.

Dopamine can influence willingness to sustain cognitive effort, but the strongest assessed human study measured effort choice rather than fatigue or performance decline over time {{cite:westbrook_dopamine_2020}}. Cognitive energy remains a multi-system outcome, and a dopamine-specific fatigue claim is unresolved.

Serotonin signalling is a core biological substrate for emotional regulation, impulse control and affective stability {{cite:shaw_emotion_2014}}. ADHD-focused serotonin reviews do not establish a uniform serotonin deficit that diet can correct {{cite:faraone_serotonin_2025}} {{cite:banerjee_does_2015}}. Tryptophan is an indispensable amino acid and the serotonin precursor. Coverage of that amino acid is not a measurement of emotional regulation, and serotonin signalling is a later step. Carbohydrate-rich versus protein-rich meals can change the plasma tryptophan-to-LNAA ratio {{cite:wurtman_effects_2003,ashley_breakfast_1985,fernstrom_lnna_2013}}. Plasma-ratio change is not serotonin signalling or an emotional-regulation benefit.

Dopamine contributes to working memory and cognitive control, but the relationship is nonlinear and depends on baseline state and whether prefrontal stability or striatal updating is required {{cite:cools_inverted-u_2011}}. ADHD imaging findings are heterogeneous across dopamine processes, regions and medication histories rather than showing a uniform dopamine deficit {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024,fusar-poli_striatal_2012}}. Meal protein supplies circulating phenylalanine, and phenylalanine can be converted to tyrosine. Tyrosine and tryptophan are precursors later catecholamine and serotonin pathways can use. These studies do not measure attention. Meal-level LNAA competition at LAT1 can shift plasma tyrosine and tryptophan ratios and, on review evidence, brain-entry bias {{cite:fernstrom_lnna_2013,ashley_breakfast_1985,wurtman_effects_2003}}. The attached meal studies do not measure attention or ADHD outcomes, and transport modulation cannot substitute for substrate sufficiency or downstream signalling. Noradrenaline helps set arousal and vigilance so attention and executive control can stay engaged {{cite:odonnell_norepinephrine_2012}}. That biological role is not a dietary-treatment claim, and ADHD imaging that varies by dopamine process does not show a uniform noradrenaline deficit or a food-based attention effect {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}.

Striatal dopamine synthesis capacity and controlled dopaminergic manipulation alter willingness to expend cognitive effort by changing benefit-versus-cost weighting, supporting a direct relationship with effort allocation rather than a general “reward chemical” account {{cite:westbrook_dopamine_2020}}. Phenylalanine from dietary protein can be converted to tyrosine, the dopamine precursor. That supply is not a measurement of motivation or drive, and it is not dopaminergic signalling. Protein-forward meals can raise the plasma tyrosine ratio relative to competing LNAAs {{cite:wurtman_effects_2003,fernstrom_lnna_2013}}. That is precursor-presentation bias, not a motivation, drive or ADHD outcome; signalling belongs downstream of this PM. Noradrenaline can change arousal and effort-related tone, but dopaminergic reward circuitry remains the primary biological driver of Motivation / Drive {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}. The attached sources do not measure motivation after a dietary change, and iron-deficiency reviews are not motivation trials {{cite:beard_iron_2003}}.

Serotonin pathways sit near positive-valence mood biology {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. Saffron supplementation trials are not serotonin-process measurements and are not a Dietary Requirement of this mechanism {{cite:jackson_effects_2021}}. Catecholamine systems can sit near reward and incentive-motivation biology, but the attached insulin–dopamine review does not measure noradrenaline signalling or a pleasure outcome after diet {{cite:gruber_impact_2023}}. Dopamine-process heterogeneity in ADHD is not a pleasure-capacity finding for this mechanism {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}.

Serotonin can interact with dopaminergic reward circuits and behavioural inhibition {{cite:faraone_serotonin_2025}}. That interaction is not a measured reward outcome after diet {{cite:tang_nutritional_2025}}.
Serotonin participates in sleep–wake and calming neurochemistry {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. Meal-level precursor transport is not a sleep outcome {{cite:fernstrom_lnna_2013}}.

Serotonin can modulate affiliative and social-affective behaviour in translational accounts {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. A saffron social-relationship outcome is not a serotonin signalling measurement {{cite:jackson_effects_2021}}.

Serotonin signalling participates in emotional processing and stress-related control {{cite:shaw_emotion_2014}}. The attached sources do not measure stress resilience after a dietary change aimed at serotonin {{cite:tang_nutritional_2025}}.

BRS1(FM4).evidence_summary: GABAergic inhibition is relevant to anxiety-related processes, providing a plausible biological connection to Apprehensive Worry. The closest human trial found that high-dose vitamin B6 reduced self-reported anxiety and strengthened an inhibitory visual assay, but it measured neither GABA nor GABA synthesis {{cite:field_high-dose_2022}}. No study here directly assessed worry, rumination or perseverative thought, while GAD65-deficient mice show sex-dependent rather than uniform anxiety-like changes {{cite:ulrich_sex_2023}}.
Efficient glutamate uptake and recycling terminate excitatory signalling {{cite:zhou_glutamate_2014}}. The attached sources do not measure cognitive-clarity outcomes in ADHD cohorts.

GABA contributes to inhibitory neural processes involved in behavioural and emotional regulation. Human studies link GABA concentrations in relevant brain regions with impulsivity and aggression {{cite:ende_impulsivity_2016}}, supporting the relevance of GABA biology to Emotional Regulation. However, these studies measure GABA concentration rather than synthesis rate {{cite:mason_decrease_2001,manor_rate_1996}}, and direct human evidence connecting GABA synthesis capacity itself with Emotional Regulation is currently lacking.

Regional glutamate/glutamine measures associate with attention scores in adults with ADHD {{cite:maltezos_glutamateglutamine_2014}}. That is a spectroscopic pool link, not measured excitatory amino-acid transporter flux. Uptake and recycling terminate excitatory signalling {{cite:zhou_glutamate_2014}}.

This mapping is translational. Limiting chronic receptor-driven energy stress could sit near recovery after load, but Clerc et al. did not measure human recovery outcomes. The relationship remains low-confidence {{cite:clerc_magnesium_2013}}.

GABAergic inhibition supports calming neurophysiology relevant to sleep and arousal balance. In adults with polysomnography-verified primary insomnia, brain GABA concentration has been compared with good sleepers in three independent samples, reporting lower, higher, and null group differences {{cite:winkelman_reduced_2008,morgan_cortical_2012,spiegelhalder_magnetic_2016}}. However, the human findings are inconsistent, and these studies measure GABA concentration rather than GABA synthesis capacity.

GABAergic regulation may influence Social Engagement indirectly through processes such as arousal and threat processing. In mice, lifelong loss of GAD65 increased preference for social interaction partners in both sexes {{cite:ulrich_sex_2023}}, opposite to a simple expectation that reduced GABA synthesis would reduce social approach. There is no human evidence linking GABA synthesis capacity to social engagement, and rodent partner preference is not equivalent to human social capacity.

This mapping is translational. Injury-level glutamate-receptor stress can sit near how systems react under load, but the attached work does not measure human stress-reactivity outcomes. Clerc et al. used a preclinical chronic receptor-stimulation model, so the relationship remains low-confidence {{cite:clerc_magnesium_2013}}.

BRS3(FM1).evidence_summary: Systemic inflammation associates with default-mode network connectivity patterns linked to perseverative thought in translational anxiety/depression framing; NF-κB transcriptional tone is the mechanism boundary. Gut–brain microbiota signalling modulates central GABA receptor expression and anxiety-related behaviour in animal models; gut-derived inflammatory load may intersect apprehensive-worry biology in anxiety/depression comorbidity framing.

Polyphenol-rich dietary patterns and lower pro-inflammatory signalling pressure may support cognitive clarity context in ADHD-relevant populations without single-nutrient outcome claims. Butyrate and gut-barrier context may reduce neuroinflammation and support brain energy metabolism — translational links to cognitive clarity without direct ADHD treatment-efficacy claims.

Systemic inflammatory signalling may intersect affective regulation framing in neurodevelopmental contexts; this PM governs transcriptional inflammatory tone only—not downstream cytokine phenotypes. Low-grade endotoxemia and sustained systemic inflammation correlate with mood instability in translational framing; gut-derived load remains the boundary of this spillover step.

Postprandial and LPS-linked inflammatory signalling intersects ADHD metabolic overlap — pattern-based anti-inflammatory meals may modulate attention-relevant inflammatory tone rather than acute NF-κB pharmacology. Propionate protected an in vitro blood–brain barrier model. That is not endotoxin translocation, and it is not an attention result. Gut microbiota studies in children remain context for this spillover step.

LPS-linked neurotransmission disruption intersects depressive mood biology in translational reviews; pro-inflammatory transcriptional tone may modulate this context without direct anhedonia-outcome claims.

Gut–brain GABAergic modulation has been linked to reduced anxiety- and depression-related behaviour in preclinical models; social-engagement outcomes remain indirect translational inference for this gut-inflammatory PM.

BRS3(FM3).evidence_summary: Persistent inflammatory signalling through IL-6- and TNF-α-linked cytokine networks is a recognised contributor to anxious and perseverative cognition within neuroimmune framing (Slavich & Irwin, 2014; Marsland et al., 2017). Human omega-3 intervention reduced inflammatory markers and anxiety symptoms alongside resolution-phase cytokine remodelling (Kiecolt-Glaser et al., 2011; Ferguson et al., 2014). This PM governs cytokine-network tone — not omega-3 treatment — and attached anxiety outcomes require one inferential step to PH016 rather than direct perseverative-thought measurement. Persistent inflammatory signalling and impaired resolution-phase lipid mediator balance are recognised contributors to anxious perseverative cognition within neuroimmune framing (Slavich & Irwin, 2014; Marsland et al., 2017). SPM-oriented resolution biology and human omega-3 intervention reduced inflammatory markers and anxiety symptoms alongside cytokine remodelling (Kiecolt-Glaser et al., 2011; Ferguson et al., 2014). This PM governs eicosanoid–SPM balance — not omega-3 treatment — and attached anxiety outcomes require one inferential step to PH016 rather than direct perseverative-thought measurement.

Postprandial inflammatory patterns in ADHD metabolic overlap may modulate cognitive clarity through cytokine-network context rather than single-mechanism claims. Specialized pro-resolving mediators actively terminate inflammation without suppressing immune surveillance — supporting cognitive clarity context through resolution-oriented lipid signalling.
Omega-3-derived resolution biology may modulate affective inflammatory context when EPA/DHA substrate and omega-6:omega-3 balance are adequate over habitual intake.

Youth ADHD cohort work reported higher hs-CRP and IL-6 with lower TNF-α, BDNF and bedtime cortisol — a mixed peripheral immune–neuroendocrine pattern rather than uniform pro-inflammatory cytokine elevation; omega-3 interventions reshape resolution-phase cytokine responses. Resolution-phase lipid mediator balance may intersect attention-relevant inflammatory tone; direct ADHD SPM outcome evidence remains limited.

Mitochondrial dysfunction is a recurrent theme in depression pathophysiology reviews; cytokine-network inflammatory tone may intersect reward-related mitochondrial biology without a direct anhedonia measurement. Resolution-phase eicosanoid balance may modulate inflammatory tone intersecting reward-processing and depressive biology in translational framing; Gruber et al. (2023) reviews insulin–dopamine reward disruption in depression as adjacent context.

BRS-X(ECS-FM1).evidence_summary: Endocannabinoid–dopamine coupling may influence behavioural activation and effort-related signalling context relevant to ADHD framing.
Omega-3-derived ethanolamides may support neuroprotective and neurogenesis-related signalling context relevant to cognitive clarity without CB1-centric framing.

Omega-3 endocannabinoidome signalling may indirectly modulate affective context through inflammatory and neuromodulatory interfaces; direct ADHD evidence remains limited. Dietary NAPE and NAE precursor biology may modulate endocannabinoidome context relevant to affective regulation; direct ADHD outcome claims remain cautious. Preserved anandamide signalling may modulate affective regulation pathways through endogenous tone rather than receptor agonism. Stress-buffering endocannabinoidome signalling may modulate affective regulation through mood-disorder-relevant endocannabinoid pathways.

Endocannabinoid signalling modulates dopaminergic reward and motivation pathways; this PM addresses neuromodulation rather than dopamine production. NAPE → NAE biosynthesis may support AEA, PEA, and OEA signalling context relevant to motivation and drive through diet-actionable endocannabinoidome pathways rather than CB1 receptor pharmacology.
Endocannabinoid-mediated stress buffering may support recovery from stress-linked neuroinflammatory and excitatory load; direct ADHD evidence remains limited.
Endocannabinoid modulation of mesolimbic dopamine signalling may influence reward regulation without equating to substance reward pharmacology.

DHEA and related omega-3 ethanolamides may intersect with anti-inflammatory and stress-buffering endocannabinoidome pathways. PEA and related NAEs may intersect with stress-buffering endocannabinoidome signalling; dietary phospholipid support remains the primary intervention frame. FAAH inhibition may preserve endogenous anandamide tone relevant to stress-buffering context; dietary polyphenols such as genistein represent plausible diet-sensitive modulation points. The endocannabinoidome appears more relevant to stress buffering than direct cognitive enhancement, integrating neuroinflammatory, HPA, and glutamatergic regulation context.

BRS-X(Hormones-FM1).evidence_summary: Oestrogen influences neural signalling systems relevant to cognitive stability across menstrual and perimenopausal contexts; ADHD-specific outcome claims should remain cautious. Altered oestrogen recycling may indirectly influence neural signalling context relevant to cognitive clarity without establishing direct single-pathway outcome certainty.

Insulin sensitivity and metabolic stability interact with reproductive hormone regulation; this PM should be framed as metabolic-endocrine integration rather than a direct ADHD treatment claim. Low testosterone states are associated with reduced energy, fatigue and reduced mental stamina, but direct ADHD-specific evidence remains limited. Microbial androgen metabolism may influence systemic androgen exposure relevant to energy and stamina context; direct ADHD evidence remains limited.

Oestrogen-mediated signalling may modulate affective regulation pathways that intersect with dopaminergic tone and stress sensitivity. The estrobolome can influence systemic oestrogen exposure through microbial beta-glucuronidase activity; downstream affective phenome effects are indirect and should not be presented as single-mechanism causal claims. Metabolic volatility may indirectly influence affective regulation through neuroendocrine and reproductive hormone coupling. Androgen signalling may influence mood and emotional regulation through interactions with multiple neural systems. Microbiome-androgen interactions may influence endocrine states relevant to mood and behavioural regulation, but direct ADHD evidence is currently limited. Butyrate-producing taxa may support endocrine and inflammatory contexts relevant to progesterone balance, but direct ADHD outcome evidence is limited.
Oestrogen influences dopaminergic and neural signalling systems relevant to executive function; direct single-mechanism ADHD outcome claims should remain cautious.

Estrobolome activity may support or disrupt oestrogen exposure depending on microbial beta-glucuronidase balance and enterohepatic recycling direction. Insulin-linked metabolic signalling and gut ecological context may modulate oestrogen-progesterone balance across feeding and stress cycles.

Testosterone signalling has been associated with motivation, effort, behavioural activation and goal-directed behaviour. Microbial androgen metabolism may influence systemic androgen availability and indirectly influence motivation-related phenomes.
Progesterone-linked calming tone may intersect with gut-derived inflammatory and SCFA signalling, but evidence for direct dietary single-mechanism effects remains limited.
Microbial SCFA context may indirectly influence stress-responsive endocrine-inflammatory tone intersecting progesterone-related stability.

BRS1(FM2).evidence_summary: Cholinergic signalling is a biological context for working-memory and cognitive precision {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}} {{cite:briguglio_dietary_2018}}. The attached sources do not measure cognitive-clarity scores after a choline change aimed at acetylcholine synthesis.

Acetylcholine is the cholinergic transmitter used in attention and learning circuits {{cite:johansson_decreased_2013}} {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. Receptor-binding differences in boys with ADHD and choline/neurodevelopment reviews supply translational context. They do not show that changing choline intake treats ADHD or raises brain acetylcholine.

BRS1(FM3).evidence_summary: DHA in neuronal phospholipids supports membrane architecture used in synaptic signalling {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}} {{cite:patrick_role_2019}}. Delivery form can change accretion in an animal model {{cite:liu_higher_2014}}. Those are structural and transport findings, not cognitive-clarity scores after a human DHA change.

Combined omega-3/6 with magnesium and zinc was followed by fewer emotional-problem scores in an observational ADHD-seeking cohort {{cite:huss_supplementation_2010}}. Membrane DHA remains the mechanism boundary; the multi-nutrient design cannot isolate incorporation {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}}.

Membrane DHA is a structural context for synaptic signalling {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}}. An observational multi-nutrient study in children seeking help for ADHD-related symptoms cannot isolate membrane DHA from co-supplemented minerals {{cite:huss_supplementation_2010}}. Omega-3 ADHD reviews remain contextual {{cite:pei-chen_chang_personalised_2021}}.

BRS2(FM1).evidence_summary: Folic acid, with or without vitamin B12, lowers blood homocysteine {{cite:collaboration_lowering_1998}}. In older adults with mild cognitive impairment, B-vitamin treatment was associated with slower cognitive decline only when omega-3 status was higher {{cite:oulhaj_omega-3_2016}}. Blood homocysteine and that combined B-vitamin interaction do not measure methionine synthase flux, and they do not establish that this reaction itself changes cognitive clarity. Lower plasma homocysteine after betaine supplements is a blood measurement, not a test of cognitive clarity or of tissue BHMT activity {{cite:olthof_low_2003}}. A choline review discusses neurodevelopment rather than an effect of this reaction on clarity {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. The relationship remains an indirect bridge with no direct outcome evidence. SAMe supplies methyl groups used by many downstream pathways relevant to neural function, but this is an inferred downstream bridge rather than evidence that MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis itself modulates Cognitive Clarity. The attached methylation review establishes SAMe's donor role, not a cognitive outcome or endogenous synthesis-flux effect {{cite:chiang_s-adenosylmethionine_1996}}. Circulating SAMe or SAM:SAH measurements cannot isolate MAT synthesis from utilisation and clearance {{cite:corrillero_bravo_analysis_2022}}. Direct relationship evidence remains a gap. SAM donates methyl groups, and homocysteine is then split between remethylation and transsulfuration {{cite:chiang_s-adenosylmethionine_1996,finkelstein_homocysteine_1998}}. Homocysteine concentration is discussed as a risk marker for cognitive decline and Alzheimer disease {{cite:luzzi_homocysteine_2022,yu_evidence-based_2020}}. Those studies measure a metabolite level. They do not measure branch rates, and they do not show that changing cycle throughput improves Cognitive Clarity.

SAMe-dependent methylation is biologically relevant to downstream neurotransmitter and membrane chemistry, but the attached mood-disorder review concerns exogenous SAMe and combined folate/B12 treatment rather than endogenous MAT activity or SAMe synthesis flux {{cite:cicero_combined_2022}}. It therefore does not directly demonstrate that this PM modulates Emotional Regulation; the relationship remains an indirect framework bridge with a direct-evidence gap.

Children with ADHD have been reported to have lower folate and vitamin B12 than comparison groups, and one cohort of boys also had higher homocysteine {{cite:razavinia_vitamins_2024,lukovac_serum_2024,wang_dietary_2019}}. Those are observational blood and diet differences. They do not show that methionine synthase activity is lower, and they do not show that folate or vitamin B12 supplementation improves attention. An MTHFR polymorphism meta-analysis concerns a folate-cycle enzyme upstream of this reaction, not methionine synthase flux {{cite:meng_association_2022}}. Reviews of ADHD diets and of choline in neurodevelopment discuss attention, but they do not test BHMT activity or betaine supplementation as an attention treatment {{cite:millichap_diet_2012,derbyshire_role_2023}}. The enzyme reaction is established separately, and a change in plasma homocysteine is not an attention outcome {{cite:evans_betaine_2002,olthof_low_2003}}. Direct evidence that this remethylation route changes Focus / Attention Stability remains a gap. Boys with ADHD had higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 than controls, and a separate case-control study linked less healthy diets with lower folate, vitamin B6 and vitamin B12 and with ADHD {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024,wang_dietary_2019}}. Those are concentration and dietary-pattern associations. They do not measure remethylation or transsulfuration rates {{cite:finkelstein_homocysteine_1998,lamers_vitamin_b6_methionine_cycle_2011}}.

BRS2(FM3).evidence_summary: SAMe-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation couples one-carbon methylation to membrane phospholipid chemistry — the methylation-dependent bridge between B-vitamin status and omega-3-enriched PC delivery toward the brain. VITACOG reanalysis, PEMT pathway biology, and phospholipid-bound DHA accretion evidence support cognitive-clarity framework translation. The findings support an association with cognitive outcomes, while the proposed causal role of methylation–membrane coupling remains unproven. Applicability to ADHD has not yet been established.

Diet and choline reviews discuss attention and neurodevelopment {{cite:millichap_diet_2012}} {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. They do not measure PEMT activity. Piglet brain DHA accretion and human cerebrospinal-fluid DHA likewise do not record this methylation {{cite:liu_higher_2014}} {{cite:arellanes_brain_2020}}. Any attention relationship is a downstream inference.

BRS3(FM2).evidence_summary: Verlaet reviews a rationale for dietary antioxidant treatment in ADHD. The human measurement is nasal defence-gene expression after a prepared sprout homogenate, not a cognitive result. Thiol/disulfide shifts and DNA oxidation markers in ADHD adults support state-sensitive redox interpretation relevant to cognitive clarity without diagnostic claims. One adult cohort had higher malondialdehyde. That marker is not a vitamin E result. Lutein is not the chain-breaking antioxidant in this membrane reaction. Synergistic antioxidant network regeneration may support cognitive clarity context in ADHD oxidative-load framing better than isolated megadose antioxidants.

Oxidative stress intersects neuroinflammatory cascades relevant to affective dysregulation framing; net redox balance is the mechanism boundary for this PM. Oxidative membrane damage and mitochondrial overlap may intersect affective regulation in neurodevelopmental framing; scope remains lipid-peroxidation control only. Network antioxidant sufficiency may indirectly modulate affective context under chronic oxidative stress; high-dose single-nutrient supplementation shows inconsistent benefit.

The human exposure changed phase II enzyme RNA in nasal cells. It does not show that ordinary repeated eating changes attention, and the sources do not compare repeated exposure with a single dose. Elevated oxidative stress indices and lipid-peroxidation markers in adult and paediatric ADHD cohorts may modulate attention-relevant redox burden when generation exceeds clearance. Lipid-peroxidation burden tracks oxidative load in ADHD cohorts; food-state antioxidant coverage may modulate membrane protection relevant to sustained attention contexts.

Nrf2-dependent detoxification and antioxidant gene programmes may intersect stress-buffering redox context; direct ADHD stress-outcome evidence remains limited. Compensatory glutathione elevation in ADHD may reflect network activity under oxidative burden; polyphenol–fibre patterns supporting urolithin A context may modulate stress-buffering redox resilience.

BRS5(FM2).evidence_summary: ADHD-focused gut–brain axis review literature synthesises microbiome ecology research gaps — indirect cognitive-clarity framing through microbial community resilience rather than measured clarity outcomes. Gut-derived polyphenol metabolites may influence mitochondrial and inflammatory resilience with downstream cognitive implications — framework translation from ADHD gut–brain research gaps rather than direct clarity-outcome measurement.

SCFA gut–brain signalling may intersect affective regulation through vagal and immune pathways — indirect translational framing from ADHD SCFA deficit observation without emotional-outcome intervention trials.

Reduced microbial alpha diversity in paediatric ADHD and lower faecal SCFA levels versus controls support ecological turnover and competitive selection as modifiable gut-community processes intersecting attention-relevant microbiome structure. ADHD cohorts showed lower faecal SCFA levels including acetic, propionic, isobutyric, isovaleric, and valeric acids versus controls — positioning microbial SCFA production and signalling as a direct observational anchor for attention-relevant gut metabolite biology.

Microbial polyphenol biotransformation generates mitophagy-relevant metabolites bridging BRS5 to BRS4 — ADHD hub evidence for this PM is indirect via gut–brain axis review context; direct ADHD urolithin-outcome trials are not in the curated set (biology > evidence gap).

BRS4(FM1).evidence_summary: The same cybrid cells respired less, which is consistent with less ATP-generating capacity in that model {{cite:verma_attention_2016}}. Cognitive energy was not measured, and the result is not a meal prescription. Cybrid cells carrying platelet mitochondria from three boys with ADHD respired less, but NAD⁺ was not measured {{cite:verma_attention_2016}}. A review of ADHD mitochondrial papers does not add an NAD⁺ measurement {{cite:ogutlu_mitochondrial_2023}}. Creatine–phosphocreatine buffering is positioned to stabilise ATP supply during changing demand. In a small crossover trial during acute sleep deprivation, a high single creatine dose altered cerebral high-energy phosphate measures and partially preserved cognitive performance {{cite:gordji-nejad_creatine_sleep_2024}}. This supports a conditional relationship under acute metabolic stress, not a universal energy effect.

Cybrid cells carrying platelet mitochondria from three boys with ADHD had lower respiration, lower complex V activity, a lower membrane potential and higher mitochondrial superoxide than control cybrids {{cite:verma_attention_2016}}. That is a small cell model. It does not show that diet changes attention.

The ADHD mitochondrial review discusses mitochondrial strain. It does not measure recovery, and it does not measure NAD⁺ {{cite:ogutlu_mitochondrial_2023}}. Rapid ATP buffering is biologically relevant to recovery after energetic demand, but the reviewed human evidence primarily measures cerebral creatine, cognition during acute stress, or clinical contexts rather than recovery capacity itself {{cite:dolan_beyond_muscle_2019}}. The relationship therefore remains indirect and evidence-limited.

BRS4(FM3).evidence_summary: Carnitine-dependent fat oxidation supports mitochondrial substrate delivery for ATP production — trial evidence in ADHD children links this transport node to functional improvement alongside behavioural endpoints. ADHD mitochondrial dysfunction reviews describe substrate-flexibility strain when oxidative phosphorylation is impaired — ketone utilisation is an indirect alternative-fuel pathway node without ADHD ketone-intervention outcomes in the hub set. Narrative synthesis of ADHD mitochondrial biomarker and oxidative-stress literature supports fuel-switching flexibility as a modifiable bioenergetic context when respiration is compromised — direct ADHD fuel-switching outcome trials remain limited.

Controlled carnitine supplementation improved behavioural and functional outcomes in children with ADHD — the strongest direct ADHD intervention anchor in BRS4, mapping fatty-acid transport into mitochondria to attention-relevant outcomes without generalising beyond trial context.

BRS6(FM1).evidence_summary: PET evidence of altered cerebral glucose metabolism in adults with hyperactivity of childhood onset and unhealthy dietary pattern associations with ADHD in case–control path analysis converge on meal-level glucose appearance kinetics as a cognitive-energy node. Altered cerebral glucose metabolism in ADHD and metabolic syndrome/insulin-resistance overlap in adult ADHD outpatients support glycaemic variability as a modifiable context for steadier cognitive fuel supply. Insulin resistance and ADHD metabolic overlap reviewed in narrative synthesis support efficient glucose disposal as a contributor to cognitive fuel stability — mechanism boundary is peripheral/metabolic insulin action, not CNS glucose transport pharmacology.

Dietary pattern linked to ADHD burden implicates postprandial glucose dynamics intersecting prefrontal and striatal fuel supply relevant to attention biology — this PM governs glucose appearance rate, not insulin disposal (PM3) or variability amplitude (PM2). Prefrontal glucose utilisation patterns in ADHD and metabolic comorbidity prevalence link glycaemic fluctuation control to attention-relevant cognitive energy availability.

BRS5(FM1).evidence_summary: The attached ADHD microbiota study did not measure intestinal permeability, tight-junction function or emotional-regulation outcomes {{cite:jiang_gut_2018}}. No direct evidence in the bounded assessment established that this PM modulates Emotional Regulation, so this remains a framework-level hypothesis with a direct-evidence gap.

Serum zonulin was associated with hyperactivity scores in one small cross-sectional ADHD study {{cite:ozyurt_increased_2018}}, but serum zonulin is an indirect barrier marker and the design cannot establish that tight-junction integrity causes attention instability. The attached microbiota-composition study did not measure permeability or tight junctions {{cite:jiang_gut_2018}}. The PM → Phenome relationship therefore remains indirect and observational. Gut microbiota profiles and an inflammatory marker have been compared with attention-related scores. [[5]](#pm-ref-5) [[7]](#pm-ref-7) Those studies did not measure lipopolysaccharide or endotoxin containment, so they do not show that this exposure mechanism changes attention. Reduced microbial alpha diversity in paediatric ADHD, compositional shifts in treatment-naïve cohorts, and open-label Bifidobacterium supplementation with symptom change converge on ecological keystone support as attention-relevant gut–brain context.

Gut microbiome composition linked to neural reward anticipation in ADHD positions keystone taxa support as a biological node intersecting motivation-relevant gut–brain signalling — not a direct reward-intervention claim.

The same studies did not measure lipopolysaccharide. [[5]](#pm-ref-5) [[7]](#pm-ref-7) They do not show that endotoxin containment changes stress reactivity. The supporting finding is recorded with Focus / Attention Stability.

BRS5(FM3).evidence_summary: Probiotic-associated symptom change in ADHD children and hypothesis-generating early-life microbial modulation windows support gut–vagal pathways intersecting affective regulation biology without definitive prevention claims.

ADHD microbiota compositional differences and lower SCFA levels imply altered microbial biotransformation of dietary precursors relevant to gut–brain neurotransmitter availability — mechanism boundary is microbial precursor processing, not BRS1 monoamine synthesis.

Microbial metabolite handling intersects reward-anticipation biology linked to gut composition in ADHD — indirect motivation framing through precursor/metabolite availability rather than direct drive-outcome trials.

Open-label Bifidobacterium bifidum supplementation associated with symptom change and altered gut microbiota in children with ADHD — vagal/ENS signalling is the proposed gut–brain conduit; early-life Lactobacillus exposure adds developmental modulation context.

BRS6(FM2).evidence_summary: Cortisol, inflammatory biomarkers, and neurotrophins measured in children and adolescents with ADHD intersect affective regulation biology through HPA-axis tone — this PM governs cortisol rhythm, not autonomic recovery (FM3).

Meta-analysis reports altered basal and morning cortisol patterns in youths with ADHD; cortisol levels in children with ADHD and sensory-over-responsivity differentiation work using cortisol markers converge on HPA rhythm as a stress-reactivity node.

BRS6(FM4).evidence_summary: Dietary pattern associations with ADHD burden and HPA dysregulation support stress-modulated reward/motivation pathways — mechanism boundary is appetite–reward drive under stress, not BRS1 catecholamine synthesis.

Metabolic-inflammatory load allocation may constrain recovery after sustained metabolic or stress challenge — indirect translation from ADHD–metabolic disorder synthesis rather than measured recovery outcomes.
Unhealthy dietary pattern linked to ADHD in case–control path analysis and altered cortisol patterns in ADHD youth intersect stress-driven appetite and reward regulation biology.

BRS2(FM2).evidence_summary: Cysteine released by cystathionine cleavage can be used later for glutathione synthesis, which is a separate mechanism. The enzyme studies do not measure recovery capacity, and they do not show that changing this conversion treats recovery {{cite:zhu_cgl_kinetics_2008,steegborn_cgl_kinetics_1999}}. Glutathione assembly supplies a thiol used in cellular redox buffering, which is relevant to recovery only as downstream biology. The human synthesis measurements are erythrocyte kinetics after combined precursor supplementation in older adults, not a recovery-outcome trial {{cite:sekhar_glutathione_2011}}. A sulfur-amino-acid-free diet slowed whole-blood synthesis while concentration was maintained {{cite:lyons_glutathione_2000}}. Higher homocysteine in boys with ADHD does not measure glutathione synthesis or recovery {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.

Homocysteine can be joined to serine and then cleaved to cysteine, but that chemistry is not evidence of a stress-reactivity effect. A study of boys with ADHD found higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12. It did not measure these enzymes, cysteine production, or stress outcomes, and it is not a treatment result {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.

The same thiol pool is a plausible contributor to stress buffering, but no assessed study tested a stress-resilience outcome {{cite:sekhar_glutathione_2011,lyons_glutathione_2000}}. The paediatric ADHD biomarker study measured homocysteine and vitamin B12, not glutathione synthesis or stress resilience {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.

BRS4(FM2).evidence_summary: Elevated glutathione and oxidative-stress markers in paediatric ADHD case–control work link mitochondrial ROS handling to redox recovery context; GSH is required for mitochondrial lactate metabolism and ROS neutralisation — this PM governs ROS production/control balance, not GSH synthesis (BRS2/BRS3).
